subject.title: [Feature]: Support Anthropic native server-side tools (web_search, web_fetch, code_execution)

question: What Anthropic server-tool contract should OpenClaw support for web_search, web_fetch, code_execution/PTC, and allowed_callers, and what opt-in/security/billing defaults must gate it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but provider-hosted code execution and delegated tool access can change tool availability, billing, transcript replay, and execution boundaries, so automation should not choose the permanent product/security contract alone.

options.title: Plugin-owned opt-in contract
options.body: Add a narrow Anthropic plugin/provider contract for server tools, default it off where execution or billing is surprising, preserve current client tools unless explicitly replaced, and require docs plus live Anthropic proof.

options.title: Web search only first
options.body: Keep this broad issue open but sponsor only the narrower Anthropic native web_search provider first, deferring web_fetch/code_execution/PTC until server-result replay and security policy are settled.

options.title: Decline provider-hosted execution
options.body: Support only read-only Anthropic server tools and reject code_execution/PTC for now because delegated provider execution is outside the desired OpenClaw security boundary.

recommendation.title: Plugin-owned opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Add a narrow Anthropic plugin/provider contract for server tools, default it off where execution or billing is surprising, preserve current client tools unless explicitly replaced, and require docs plus live Anthropic proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the latest maintainer-review context on this issue and recent broad touches across the Anthropic transport/config surface.
